aiken/merkle_patricia_forestry/Neighbor.title: Neighbor
aiken/merkle_patricia_forestry/Neighbor.description: since | 1.0.0 --- | --- A neighbor node used in a proof. See [Proof](#Proof) for details.

aiken/merkle_patricia_forestry/ProofStep.title: ProofStep
aiken/merkle_patricia_forestry/ProofStep.description: since | 1.0.0 --- | --- We distinguish three kind of proof steps: Branch, Fork and Leaf. Each step contains a `skip` value which corresponds to the length of the common prefix at that particular level. The details of each level is documented [in the wiki :: Proof Format](https://github.com/aiken-lang/merkle-patricia-forestry/wiki/Proof-format).

cardano/address/Address.title: Address
cardano/address/Address.description:
A Cardano `Address` typically holding one or two credential references.

 Note that legacy bootstrap addresses (a.k.a. 'Byron addresses') are
 completely excluded from Plutus contexts. Thus, from an on-chain
 perspective only exists addresses of type 00, 01, ..., 07 as detailed
 in [CIP-0019 :: Shelley Addresses](https://github.com/cardano-foundation/CIPs/tree/master/CIP-0019/#shelley-addresses).

cardano/address/Credential.title: Credential
cardano/address/Credential.description:
A general structure for representing an on-chain `Credential`.

 Credentials are always one of two kinds: a direct public/private key
 pair, or a script (native or Plutus).

cardano/address/PaymentCredential.title: PaymentCredential
cardano/address/PaymentCredential.description:
A general structure for representing an on-chain `Credential`.

 Credentials are always one of two kinds: a direct public/private key
 pair, or a script (native or Plutus).

cardano/address/StakeCredential.title: StakeCredential
cardano/address/StakeCredential.description:
Represent a type of object that can be represented either inline (by hash)
 or via a reference (i.e. a pointer to an on-chain location).

 This is mainly use for capturing pointers to a stake credential
 registration certificate in the case of so-called pointer addresses.

cardano/transaction/OutputReference.title: OutputReference
cardano/transaction/OutputReference.description:
An `OutputReference` is a unique reference to an output on-chain. The `output_index`
 corresponds to the position in the output list of the transaction (identified by its id)
 that produced that output

cardano_keri/application/action/Action.title: Action
cardano_keri/application/action/Action.description: An operation that brings an output into being, listed in the mint redeemer.

anyOf.title: CreateConfiguration
anyOf.description:
Create the configuration record of `registry` in the output at
 `output_index`, in the transaction that spends `seed`.

anyOf.title: BookRegistration
anyOf.description: Book the registration held by the output at `output_index`.

anyOf.title: BookTermination
anyOf.description:
Book the termination of `key` in `registry`: the output at `output_index`
 is the termination request, and `pending` is the convicted checkpoint's
 pending output it spends.

cardano_keri/bounty_commitment/BountyMin.title: BountyMint
cardano_keri/bounty_commitment/BountyMin.description: Minting redeemer of the commitment program.

cardano_keri/bounty_commitment/BountyRev.title: BountyRevealV1
cardano_keri/bounty_commitment/BountyRev.description: `DAT-271-REVEAL`. The evidence is not duplicated here.

cardano_keri/bounty_commitment/BountySpe.title: BountySpend
cardano_keri/bounty_commitment/BountySpe.description: Spending redeemer of the commitment program.

cardano_keri/bounty_commitment/Commitmen.title: CommitmentFamily
cardano_keri/bounty_commitment/Commitmen.description:
Deployment identity of the applied program. The #254 registry and the
 enforcement observer name the policy through this record; the script
 itself learns its policy from the ledger context instead, because
 embedding its own hash as a parameter would be circular.

cardano_keri/bounty_commitment/Commitmen.title: CommitmentParameters
cardano_keri/bounty_commitment/Commitmen.description:
`DAT-271-PARAMETERS`, applied magnitudes only. No ambient manifest
 lookup and no protocol default: every value, including the release
 lifetime, is an explicit argument of the applied program.

cardano_keri/consumer/Context.title: Context
cardano_keri/consumer/Context.description: Lean `Context`: fixed by the relying contract.

cardano_keri/endpoint_board_authorizatio.title: AuthorizedBoardDatum
cardano_keri/endpoint_board_authorizatio.description:
The authorized endpoint-board wire datum.

 The shape is released protocol data, not an implementation detail: it must
 stay `Constr 0` with exactly these six fields in this order. The frozen
 four-field `BoardDatumV1` of `endpoint_board_types` shares the constructor
 index and is distinguished from this one by field count alone.

cardano_keri/endpoint_board_authorizatio.title: BoardNonce
cardano_keri/endpoint_board_authorizatio.description:
The one-use ledger output reference bound into an authorization.

 Wire shape: `Constr 0 [B nonce_tx_id, I nonce_output_index]`, which is
 exactly the ledger's own `OutputReference` encoding.

cardano_keri/m12/types/EscrowAction.title: EscrowAction
cardano_keri/m12/types/EscrowAction.description: Escrow skeleton actions: witnessed service or notice close.

cardano_keri/m12/types/EvidenceGrade.title: EvidenceGrade
cardano_keri/m12/types/EvidenceGrade.description: Witness-quality grade used by cursor, escrow, and predicates.

cardano_keri/m12/types/KeriState.title: KeriState
cardano_keri/m12/types/KeriState.description: Adopted KERI projection used by the cursor and predicates.

cardano_keri/m12/types/LineageAction.title: LineageAction
cardano_keri/m12/types/LineageAction.description: Lineage skeleton actions: genesis, successor, or close marker.

cardano_keri/migration/types/MigrationRo.title: MigrationRole
cardano_keri/migration/types/MigrationRo.description:
Which live lifecycle position a migration moves. The terminal burn state
 is deliberately absent: it is an end state, not something that can be
 migrated, so it is unrepresentable here rather than merely unused. `Board`
 is the board-side position; its state and inventory rules belong to
 S254-2, never to this module.

anyOf.title: CheckpointFrozen
anyOf.description:
Kept so that `Board` keeps its constructor index, which the endpoint
 board's migration wire shares; the checkpoint no longer has this role.

anyOf.title: CheckpointArmed
anyOf.description: Kept so that `Board` keeps its constructor index (see above).

cardano_keri/migration/types/MigrationTa.title: MigrationTarget
cardano_keri/migration/types/MigrationTa.description:
Where a migration lands (DAT-254-TARGET). `legacy_refund_address` is
 optional and legacy-only: it names where value from a retired generation
 is returned, and is `None` for every target that has no legacy remainder.

hash_proof/HashProofRedeemer.title: HashProofRedeemer
hash_proof/HashProofRedeemer.description:
The Tx-A redeemer: the FINAL keripy `icp` serialization, the raw
 32-byte AID digest, and the offsets of the 44-char `i` and `d` value
 spans inside it (keripy's field order `v,t,d,i,...` is fixed, so the
 `d` span always precedes the `i` span — H1 encodes that ordering).

singular_state/preimage/RegistryIdentity.title: RegistryIdentity
singular_state/preimage/RegistryIdentity.description: The identity of a registry: its state token.

token_lib/TokenId.title: TokenId
token_lib/TokenId.description:
Helper functions for token handling in the MPF Cage validator.

 This module provides utilities for:
 - Token identification and extraction from values
 - Asset name computation from output references
 - Value construction for single tokens

 ## Role in the Cage System

 The cage validator needs to identify, extract, and manipulate
 single NFTs. This module provides the plumbing:

 - `assetName`: Derives a unique, deterministic asset name from an
   `OutputReference` using SHA2-256. This is the foundation of the
   cage minting policy's uniqueness guarantee.

 - `tokenFromValue`: Extracts the single non-ADA token from a value.
   Used to identify which caged token a UTxO belongs to.

 - `quantity`: Checks how many of a specific token exist in a value.
   Used during minting validation to ensure exactly 1 token is minted.

 - `valueFromToken`: Constructs a value with exactly 1 of a token.
   Used in tests and when building expected output values.

 ## Design Decisions

 `TokenId` only contains the `assetName`, not the `PolicyId`. This is
 because the policy ID is always the cage script's own hash, which is
 available from context. Separating them avoids redundancy and makes
 it easier to compare tokens across different operations.

 ## Test Hints
 - `assetName` is deterministic: same OutputReference always produces
   same asset name
 - `assetName` is collision-resistant: different OutputReferences produce
   different asset names (SHA2-256 property)
 - `tokenFromValue` returns None for ADA-only values
 - `tokenFromValue` returns None for multi-policy values
 - `tokenFromValue` returns None for multi-asset-name values under one policy
 - `quantity` returns None when the policy or asset name is absent
 A unique identifier for a token, consisting of just the asset name.

 The policy ID is provided separately in functions that need it,
 allowing the same TokenId to be used across different contexts.

 ## Why Only AssetName
 In the cage system, the policy ID is always the cage script's own
 hash (since it's a combined minting+spending validator). By storing
 only the asset name, we avoid carrying redundant policy ID references
 through the datum structures. The asset name alone uniquely identifies
 a caged token within the cage script's namespace.

 ## Derivation
 The asset name is derived from an OutputReference via `assetName()`.
 It is the SHA2-256 hash of (transaction_id ++ output_index_as_2_bytes).

token_types/Migration.title: Migration
token_types/Migration.description:
Migration of a cage thread token from the pinned predecessor policy to this
 cage policy. The predecessor policy is a `mpfCage` validator parameter (not a
 caller-supplied field), so an attacker-created predecessor cannot satisfy the
 migration by construction.

token_types/OwnerAuth.title: OwnerAuth
token_types/OwnerAuth.description:
Owner authorization for a value-write operation.
 Proves the requester controls the AID registered in the identity trie.

fields.title: owner_aid
fields.description: Key in the identity_root MPF trie identifying this AID.

fields.title: owner_key
fields.description:
Raw Ed25519 public key (32 bytes). blake2b_256(owner_key) must match
 the value at owner_aid in the identity trie.

fields.title: owner_sig
fields.description: Ed25519 signature (64 bytes) over blake2b_256(domain ++ request_out_ref).

anyOf.title: UpdateAction
anyOf.description:
Apply the request's MPF operation using value_proof, after verifying
 the owner's identity and signature via auth.

anyOf.title: Rejected
anyOf.description: Reject the request (expiry or dishonest timestamp).

fields.title: root
fields.description: Current MPF root of the value trie.

fields.title: identity_root
fields.description:
Snapshot of the AID identity registry MPF root.
 Maps owner_aid -> blake2b_256(cur_pubkey).
 Oracle may update this field in the Modify output datum.
